title: Elliptic Curve Cryptosystems
shortLabel: Elliptic curve cryptosystems and primitive points
plainSummary: Introduces elliptic curve public-key cryptosystems unconditionally, mentioning Hooley's and Serre's GRH primitive-point bounds only as background motivation.
plainImpactUpgrade: A checked proof of Dirichlet GRH does not settle the elliptic-curve Artin-type questions, which rest on Chebotarev and elliptic curve L-functions beyond Dirichlet characters.
plainFallbackNote: The paper's own nonsmoothness density theorem is proved unconditionally via the Chebotarev density theorem, needing no Riemann hypothesis.

title: PRIMES is in P
authors: Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, Nitin Saxena
plainSummary: The paper gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether any given integer is prime or composite without unproved assumptions.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH changes nothing here, since the AKS algorithm is already unconditional.
plainFallbackNote: The paper itself is the unconditional algorithm; earlier conditional methods like Miller's test under ERH are only historical background.

title: On Artin's conjecture
plainSummary: Hooley proves Artin's conjecture that a fixed integer is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer number fields.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of classical RH plus Dirichlet GRH does not supply the number-field Dedekind zeta hypothesis Hooley needs, so Artin's conjecture remains open.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional proof of Artin's primitive root conjecture is known; Hooley's result is purely conditional on the number-field GRH.
extractedQuote: In 1967, Hooley showed GRH for Dedekind zeta-functions of all number fields Q(a^{1/n}, zeta_n) implies Artin's primitive root conjecture in its quantitative form.

title: Explicit bounds for primality testing and related problems
plainSummary: Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, every proper subgroup of the units modulo m misses some small integer below two log-squared m, giving explicit primality witness bounds.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of Dirichlet GRH would make these deterministic primality witness bounds unconditional theorems.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditional primality testing exists via other methods (e.g., later AKS), but this paper proves no unconditional version of its GRH-conditional bound.

title: Computing images of Galois representations attached to elliptic curves
plainSummary: The paper gives randomized algorithms that compute the Galois image on elliptic curve torsion, with polynomial running times under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for number fields.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH plus Dirichlet GRH does not help here, since the algorithms rely on the Dedekind zeta GRH for number fields via effective Chebotarev bounds.
plainFallbackNote: The algorithms can be run unconditionally, but their running times then increase from polynomial to exponential.
extractedQuote: By the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) we refer to the assumption that the non-trivial zeros of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field all lie on the critical line {s∈C:Re(s)=1/2}.

title: Simple Zeros of the Riemann Zeta-Function
authors: J. Brian Conrey, Amit Ghosh, S. M. Gonek
plainSummary: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Lindelöf Hypothesis, at least 70 percent of zeta zeros are simple and 84 percent distinct.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked RH alone would not settle this theorem, since it also needs the unproved Generalized Lindelöf Hypothesis.
plainFallbackNote: No unconditional lower bound on the proportion of simple zeros is proved here; prior conditional results remain the benchmark.
extractedQuote: Here we prove by a new method that if the Riemann and Generalized Lindelöof Hypotheses hold, then at least 70.3704 percent of the zeros are simple and at least 84.5679 percent are distinct.

title: On Artin's conjecture
plainSummary: Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the paper proves Artin's conjecture on primitive roots for a positive proportion of primes.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked RH plus Dirichlet GRH proof does not settle this, since Artin's conjecture needs the generalized Riemann hypothesis for number-field Dedekind zeta functions.
plainFallbackNote: Unconditionally, Hooley-style density results and later unconditional positive-proportion results for Artin primes exist, but the full conjecture remains open.
extractedQuote: On Artin's conjecture

title: Serre's uniformity problem in the split Cartan case
plainSummary: The paper proves unconditionally that for large primes p, rational points on the split Cartan modular curve are only cusps and CM points, partially resolving Serre's uniformity question.
plainImpactUpgrade: A machine-checked proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH changes nothing here, since the main theorem is already unconditional; GRH appears only in discussion of earlier work.
plainFallbackNote: No conditional hypothesis is needed: the paper itself supplies the unconditional proof of its main theorem.
extractedQuote: We prove that there exists an integer $p_{0}$ such that $X_{\mathrm{split}} (p)(\Bbb{Q} )$ is made of cusps and CM-points for any prime ${p>p_0}$.
